title: Count what was checked, not what was filled
statement: Count what was checked, not what was filled: a populated answer, score or 'verified' field says nothing about whether the content is right or whether anyone reviewed it.
example: One report on 4,165 extracted questions turned an answer field filled for 99.7% of them into a claim that 99.7% have correct answers.
detail: A report on 4,165 questions extracted from 1,993 PDF resources presented field population as quality: an answer field filled for 99.7% of questions became "99.7% have correct answers", and the summary claimed 99.9%+ accuracy in core educational data (`icloud-work/incept/input-generator/UAE_EDUCATIONAL_ANALYSIS_FINAL_REPORT.md`). Its human-verified field was 100% populated although the schema gives it a default of false, so the count shows a filled field, not a review.

evidence.quote: - Achieved 99.9%+ accuracy in core educational data
Do not seed a “correct” saved record to prove a real semantic result.
This is not 346 completed student interactions.
Source answers, intended keys, page arrival and enabled Next alone do not count.
These captures are not 1439 independent tests.
Field coverage and correct source paths do not prove the explanation is true.
Stored phase is not evidence of mastery
I’ll check against what you asked for, rather than trusting the tasks’ “completed” status.
Human disposition exists only when an authorized account explicitly changes its own review status; passive activity never creates one.
A populated media folder is not proof that the final video contains speech.
An item-bank count is not proof that any of those conditions hold.
